renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: cazyme_hierarchy
  title: CAZy class, family and substrate
  description: |-
    Each arc is a group of CAZyme genes: the inner ring is the CAZy class, the middle ring the family and the outer ring the predicted substrate, sized by the number of genes and coloured by class. It answers which enzyme classes and families dominate and what they are predicted to act on.
    How to read: a wide arc is a class or family that many genes carry. A large share of genes under an unassigned substrate means the substrate prediction covers little of the set. Click an arc to zoom in on it.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: cazy_class
  roles:
    ranks:
    - cazy_class
    - family
    - substrate
    abundance: genes

- component: figure
  title: CAZyme classes per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split by the CAZy class of its CAZyme genes. It answers how large the CAZyme repertoire of each sample is and how it divides between glycoside hydrolases, glycosyltransferases and the other classes.
    How to read: a taller bar is a larger repertoire, which also follows depth and assembly size. Compare the colour shares between samples to see a shift in enzyme classes.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: genes
    color: cazy_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      genes: CAZyme genes
      cazy_class: CAZy class

- component: card
  title: CAZyme genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of predicted CAZyme genes, and the ring splits them by CAZy class. It answers how many carbohydrate-active enzymes were found and which classes they belong to.
    How to read: a class that is absent or unexpectedly large is worth checking against the sample type.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  column: genes
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cazy_class
  caption: genes, by CAZy class

- component: card
  title: Distinct CAZy families
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct CAZy families found, and the bars rank the CAZy classes by how many families each holds. It answers how diverse the enzyme set is.
    How to read: a class with many families is the more diverse one. Compare with the gene count: many genes in few families means redundancy.
  column: family
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cazy_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: classes with the most distinct families
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Genes with a predicted substrate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of CAZyme genes that have a predicted substrate, and the bar splits them by substrate. It answers which carbohydrates the predicted enzymes act on.
    How to read: a dominant substrate points at what the community degrades most. Genes without a substrate are left out, so the count is lower than the total number of CAZyme genes.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  column: genes
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: substrate
  filter_expr: col('substrate') != 'unassigned'
  caption: genes, by predicted substrate

- component: card
  title: Tools agreeing on a gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of tools, out of the three of run_dbCAN, that call the same gene a CAZyme, and the strip compares it with 2. It answers how confident the annotation is.
    How to read: genes called by all three tools are the safest. A low average means many calls rest on one tool and may be false.
    Lines and annotations: the threshold is 2 tools. The dbCAN2 paper combines the tools and removes the CAZymes found by only one of them to improve accuracy.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29771380/
  column: n_tools
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 2.0
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: average tools agreeing, against 2

- component: table
  title: CAZyme genes
  description: |-
    Each row is a predicted CAZyme gene, with the family each of the three tools called, how many agree, the resolved family, its class, its substrate and its EC number. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: filter by substrate or family to list the genes behind a bar, or sort by the tools column to inspect the weakest calls.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: family

- component: figure
  title: Predicted substrates per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a predicted substrate, with the number of CAZyme gene clusters that point at it, split by sample. It answers which carbohydrates the clusters of each sample are predicted to process.
    How to read: a tall bar is a substrate many clusters target. A substrate that one sample holds alone marks a difference in degradation potential between samples.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: substrate
    y: clusters
    color: sample
    labels:
      substrate: Predicted substrate
      clusters: Gene clusters
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: CAZyme gene clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of CAZyme gene clusters with a predicted substrate, and the bars rank the substrates by the clusters that target them. It answers how many clusters have a substrate and which ones dominate.
    How to read: the leading substrate is what the community degrades most. run_dbCAN prefers the dbCAN-PUL homology call over the dbCAN-sub majority vote when both exist.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  column: clusters
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: substrate
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: substrates with the most clusters

- component: card
  title: Homology support of substrate calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the summed bit scores of the homologous gene pairs between a cluster and its best dbCAN-PUL hit, and the box shows the spread. It answers how strong the homology behind a substrate call is.
    How to read: a high score means the cluster resembles a characterised polysaccharide utilization locus over several genes. A low score is a tentative call, to read with the majority-vote column of the table.
    Note: the run_dbCAN documentation describes this value as a sum and publishes no minimum score, so no cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html
  column: bitscore
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: CAZyme gene clusters
  description: |-
    Each row is a CAZyme gene cluster, with its contig, its best dbCAN-PUL hit and substrate, the homology score, and the substrate and score of the dbCAN-sub majority vote. It answers the exact detail behind every other tile.
    How to read: compare the two substrate calls of a cluster. When they differ, the documentation recommends the dbCAN-PUL call first.
    Source: https://dbcan.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/run_from_raw_reads.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cazyme_upset
  title: Agreement between the three tools
  description: |-
    Each bar is a combination of annotation tools, with the number of genes that exactly those tools called a CAZyme, and the dots below say which tools are in the combination. It answers how often the three run_dbCAN tools agree.
    How to read: a tall bar on all three dots is a gene every tool confirms. Bars on a single dot are genes only one tool called, the weakest calls. Bars are coloured by the number of tools in the combination.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. The dbCAN2 paper combined its tools and removed the CAZymes found by only one of them to improve accuracy, so the bars with two or three dots are the calls the combination supports.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29771380/
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    set_columns:
    - hmmer
    - dbcan_sub
    - diamond
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: table
  title: Tool membership per gene
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene, with a 1 under each tool that reported a CAZy family for it and a 0 otherwise. It answers which tools back a given gene.
    How to read: filter on a tool column to list the genes it reports alone.
